outcome: Clinically severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection (SARI-WI)
cohort: Infants born between 2014 and 2018 at Hospices Civils de Lyon, France, who were followed up to 1 year of age.
finding: Infants born just before or within the early weeks of the RSV epidemic (e.g., November, October) were at significantly higher risk for severe RSV infection, with factors like term birth, vaginal delivery, and absence of siblings modifying this risk.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery, when combined with term birth and the absence of siblings, was associated with a very low likelihood of severe RSV infection for infants born in months other than October or November.
